description:
FILED s473t5f (#1501 round 7, uni/, 2026-09-13).  PRE-EXISTING; ASCII-probed.

`\$!` takes a reference to the MAGIC scalar, so every read THROUGH the
reference re-runs get-magic and sees the CURRENT errno.  PCL's `\$!` captures
the VALUE at the moment the reference is taken:

    $! = 2;  my $r = \$!;  $! = 1;
    print "${$r}", " | ", "$!", "\n";

    perl: Operation not permitted | Operation not permitted
    PCL : No such file or directory | Operation not permitted

The direct read of `$!` is right on both -- it is only the path through the
reference that is frozen.  Blessing the reference (`bless \$!, 'Ff'`) makes no
difference, which is the shape the live row uses.

WHAT IT COSTS: `t/uni/bless.t` row 81 -- its "ref is ref to magic" block,
`$! = 2; $f1 = bless \$!, "á¸"; $! = 1; $f1->test;` where `test` asserts
`${$_[0]}` is errno 1's string.  ONE row, and it is the file's only failure.

THE FAMILY: this is the magic-scalar half of the box model -- the same
question `reference_box_magic_hook` (memory) and the tie FETCH work answer for
other paths.  `$!` already has a getter on the direct path (PCL prints the
right string for `"$!"`), so what is missing is that `p-backslash` on a magic
scalar must produce a reference that DEFERS to that getter rather than a
reference to a snapshot box.  Every magic scalar with a getter has the same
hole (`$0`, `$@` after a later die, the `$^`-family), so a fix here is one
mechanism, not one variable -- probe two more before designing.
subject: a reference to a MAGIC scalar freezes its value: `$!=2; $r=\$!; $!=1; ${$r}` is errno 1 in perl and errno 2 in PCL -- t/uni/bless.t row 81, and the same hole for every magic scalar with a getter
